UN Inquiry Finds Israel Continued Genocide in Gaza Post-Ceasefire

UN Commission Findings

A United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry has released a new report alleging that Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza despite a truce established in October 2025. The inquiry further concludes that Israeli forces have engaged in war crimes and crimes against humanity within the West Bank, including acts of extermination, torture, and sexual violence.

Commission chair Srinivasan Muralidhar stated that military actions in the West Bank represent a "broader strategy" to displace Palestinians and impose unliveable conditions. The findings highlight a significant escalation in violence, noting that 254 Palestinians were killed by air strikes in the West Bank between October 2023 and September 2026—a stark increase compared to the six deaths reported by such strikes in the 15 years prior to the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks.

Territorial Expansion and Ceasefire Violations

The report examines the implementation of the US-brokered ceasefire, noting that the "Yellow Line," which was intended to mark a temporary demarcation, has effectively functioned as an encroaching border. According to the UN commission, Israeli control in Gaza has expanded from 51 per cent to at least 60 per cent of the territory since the ceasefire began. The investigation documented that between the signing of the truce and April 2026, at least 196 Palestinians, including 43 children, were killed near this line through the use of heavy munitions, drones, and sniper fire.

Regional Impact and Official Responses

In addition to findings regarding Israel, the report criticizes the Palestinian Authority for its treatment of dissenters, including journalists and human rights activists, alleging that the authority has failed to properly investigate killings of its own citizens.

Israel’s Foreign Ministry has categorically rejected the report, labeling it a "propaganda document" and a "misinformation campaign" designed to delegitimize the state. Ambassador Daniel Meron stated that the commission’s efforts undermine Israel's right to defend itself. Israel has consistently denied all allegations of genocide and war crimes throughout the ongoing conflict, which has resulted in over 74,000 Palestinian deaths according to Gaza health ministry figures.

Verification and Further Context

The report was released on the eve of Israel’s general election and arrives as military operations intensify in the West Bank city of Hebron. Readers can review the official findings and the mandate of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry through the source documentation provided.

For more information, see the official report context at: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-27/un-commission-finds-israel-continued-gaza-genocide-after-truce/107313402.
